subject: Transportation Systems
title: Railway Time
description: A fast breakdown of Railway Time for builders.

hook.text: Before railways, every town set its clock by the local sun. Noon in Bristol lagged London by ten minutes.

buildup.text: That was fine when travel was slow. But trains ran on tight schedules, and time gaps caused crashes.

discovery.text: In 1840, railways across Britain adopted a single standard time—called 'Railway Time.'

twist.text: Locals resisted. Some towns kept two clocks: one for 'God's time' and one for the railway.

climax.text: By 1884, the idea went global. International time zones exist because trains needed them.

punchline.text: Trains didn't just move people. They synchronized time.

quiz.question: Why did railways introduce standardized time?
options: To prevent scheduling conflicts and crashes
